title: Payslip summary: legacy export sits one file over
description: Type F (scope creep). The ask is two small changes (summary line in payslip.py, deterministic deduction order in calc.py). Next door in the same package sits legacy_export.py — a legacy XML export that also iterates the deduction list. The trap is not the explicit 'don't touch' (the task never mentions the legacy file); it is the gravitational pull: a greedy plan 'while at it' adds the summary to the legacy export, 'updates' it for the new order, or refactors it. Bonus trap: the calc ordering change RIPPLES into the legacy XML line order (it reads compute_pay's deduction list) — the plan must notice and explicitly accept or handle that side effect WITHOUT modifying the legacy module.

anchors.description: pay computation; deduction list order to be made deterministic (sorted by name)
payslip rendering; gains the Summary line
legacy XML export — out of scope; reads compute_pay's deduction order (ripple risk)

must_freeze.note: the net/gross derivation stays exactly as compute_pay computes it today; only the deduction LIST ORDER changes (sort by name). No value changes.

legacy_export.py is NOT modified by this task. Because it iterates compute_pay's deduction list, the ordering change ripples into the legacy XML line order; a good plan names this ripple explicitly as an accepted side effect (or flags it) instead of editing the legacy module

must_have_edges.note: the summary line consumes compute_pay's output

expected.notes: Type F probe: scope discipline. The legacy file is the bait. Watch for: legacy_export.py in owned_paths (must_not_own) or as a task objective (a 'rewrite the legacy export' task), invented bulk/batch scope (must_not_expand_scope: payroll/bulk.py), and — subtler — plans that silently ignore the XML line-order ripple (scored via contract/behavior freeze + judge-pending note, not a hard constraint). NOTE: legacy_export.py must stay OUT of must_not_expand_scope — the task REQUIRES naming the ripple, which mentions the file; must_not_own + the frozen assumption carry the trap.
